correctness.rationale: The partials are x_(j−1)^2, giving smoothness. On a rational subspace the ordered coefficients of the cubic restriction in t_a^2 t_b are precisely B(b_a,b_b); binary point containment alone would not suffice. The orthogonal splitting T⊕E yields six Q-null two-spaces in E, three in each of two disjoint-nonzero-vector partitions, so no Q-null three-space exists (each nonzero vector lies on two, rather than three, null two-spaces). The graphs over the six spaces, and the subspaces meeting T in a line of vector dimension one, give 75 lines and nine planes. For the point degrees, a nonzero t in T lies on nine vertical lines; at a nonzero pure e in E there are three vertical and four graph lines; at t+e with both components nonzero there are one vertical, two rank-one graph, and two isomorphism graph lines. An independent RREF enumeration of 63, 651 and 1395 candidate spaces evaluated the original cubic on every candidate over F4, not just the nine positives. This is exact by interpolation since the restriction has individual degrees ≤3<4. It matched 39,75,9, all four histograms, and a common point for each row triple and a common line for each column triple, with each row and column meeting in exactly one plane. Replay: python3 /workspace/reproductions/audit_klein_f2.py.
residual_risks: No count over proper extensions or over the algebraic closure is made. F4 evaluation here certifies only the restriction of the cubic on subspaces defined over F2.

evidence: The 2025 census enumerates all 3,718,649 F2-projective classes and computes complete line and plane sets on every class. The older DLR zeta formula and oddness result for rational lines are broader but do not alone give the individual data.

originality.rationale: Auel–Kulkarni–Petok–Weinbaum, Math. Comp. 94 (2025), §§3.3–3.4, compute the complete sets of F2-lines and F2-planes for every F2-isomorphism class of cubic fourfolds, including this smooth cyclic fourfold. These are subspaces with coordinates, not merely aggregate counts. The exact sizes, intersection grid, and line/point incidence degrees are determined by intersecting or testing containment among the already enumerated spaces. The short bilinear proof and naming of grid rows and columns do not make the census or its incidence data an uncovered mathematical claim.
residual_risks: No exact row labelled Klein was retrieved in the published catalogue; coverage is by the stronger complete set computation, not a claim that the term nine-plane grid occurs in print.

value.rationale: The arithmetic configuration is natural and the orthogonal-splitting proof is a useful way to explain it, but the frozen finding is a census and elementary incidence extraction for one form from an existing complete geometric census. It does not establish a distinct nonmechanical invariant, beyond this extraction, to sustain the claimed contribution.
residual_risks: This is a value judgment on this frozen claim, not on potential new results about twists or bilinear geometries beyond this catalogue.
